best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of a season cut dramatically short. These productions, which debuted in the brief window before the industry's historic shutdown, continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Leading our selection is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, where a grittier production approach has earned strong critical acclaim, even as some purists remain skeptical of the changes. This revival demonstrates how classic material can be reexamined for contemporary audiences without losing its essential power.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as another highlight, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a stellar production that proves the work's examination of race, identity, and military life remains urgently relevant decades after it was written. The show's critical reception underscores the value of finally bringing overlooked American classics to the Broadway stage.

Other notable entries include **Grand Horizons**, a well-crafted boulevard comedy elevated by performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, and Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, which divides critics between those captivated by her luminous performance and those who question the theatrical adaptation itself.

Rounding out the selection is Ivo van Hove's polarizing **West Side Story**, a radical reimagining that challenges traditional approaches to the beloved musical with striking video design and fresh interpretive choices.

With an average critical score of 75/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 offers diverse theatrical experiences worth exploring for anyone interested in how Broadway balances tradition with innovation.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—productions that not only marked the industry's resilient return from pandemic shutdown but also pushed artistic boundaries in unexpected directions.

The class of 2021 demonstrates exceptional quality, with our featured shows averaging an impressive 81/100 critical score. Leading the pack is "Dana H.," Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance that critics describe as mesmerizing and unforgettable. Close behind, "The Phantom of the Opera" proves Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical remains a spectacular experience, while "Lackawanna Blues" showcases Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic solo performance embodying dozens of characters from his childhood.

The year's offerings reveal Broadway's creative diversity: verbatim theater transforms FBI transcripts into gripping drama with "Is This a Room," while "Pass Over" blends Beckett and Exodus to examine Black American experience. Epic storytelling reaches new heights with "The Lehman Trilogy," and immersive theater redefines the space itself in "Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club." Gender-swapped reimaginings breathe new life into Sondheim's "Company," pop sensibilities energize historical narrative in "SIX," and Lynn Nottage's "Clyde's" finds warmth and redemption in a truck-stop sandwich shop.

Together, these productions capture a pivotal moment when Broadway reopened with both commercial stalwarts and bold experimental works, proving the medium's enduring vitality and capacity for reinvention. Whether you're seeking theatrical innovation or timeless spectacle, the 2021 season offers compelling options that continue to resonate with audiences today.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of a season dramatically cut short by global events. Despite the truncated run, several productions managed to make lasting impressions on critics and audiences before theaters went dark.

Leading our selection is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, where this grittier reboot earns an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its darker vision, though the production remains divisive among purists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** finally receives its long-overdue Broadway debut in a stellar revival that proves Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama about racism in the military has lost none of its searing relevance, earning a 78/100 across 29 reviews.

The season offered variety beyond these heavyweight productions. **Grand Horizons** provides boulevard comedy comfort with its story of a divorcing elderly couple, elevated considerably by performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Meanwhile, Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics between those mesmerized by her luminous performance and those who find the adaptation itself too static for the stage. Rounding out our selection, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves predictably polarizing, with its bold video design and visceral staging earning both passionate advocates and fierce detractors.

With an average critic score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 plays demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, even in a season that never reached its full potential. Explore each show's detailed reviews and audience reactions to discover which of these productions resonates with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a watershed moment for American theater—a year when stages reopened after pandemic shutdowns and artists responded with some of the most daring, innovative work in recent memory.

The ten productions featured here average an impressive 81/100 critical score, reflecting both the quality of the work and the industry's determination to return with purpose. Leading the field is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real interview with his mother about her kidnapping. Critics consistently describe it as unforgettable, even as they grapple with its challenging format.

The year's offerings span remarkable range: from **The Lehman Trilogy**'s epic three-hour examination of American capitalism to intimate solo performances like Ruben Santiago-Hudson's **Lackawanna Blues**. Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over** earned particular significance as Broadway's official reopening production, bringing urgent commentary on Black American life through a lens that blends Beckett with the Book of Exodus.

These 2021 plays also demonstrate Broadway's embrace of theatrical experimentation—from the verbatim FBI transcript of **Is This a Room** to the immersive environmental staging of **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**. Even established titles like **The Phantom of the Opera** and **Company** find renewed relevance through fresh interpretations.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting past favorites, this guide offers insight into a pivotal year that redefined what Broadway plays could achieve.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the class of 2022 stands out as a remarkable year for Broadway drama and musical theater, marked by intimate storytelling, vital revivals, and bold new voices.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenager with a rapid-aging condition that critics consistently hail as a near-perfect achievement. The show balances laugh-out-loud comedy with profound emotional depth, earning an impressive 88/100 across 34 reviews. Close behind is **Into the Woods**, a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as both a triumphant tribute to the late composer and a testament to the enduring power of his work, with stellar performances that reinvigorate this classic fairy tale deconstruction.

The year also proved to be a watershed moment for Pulitzer Prize-winning works making their way to Broadway stages. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original meta-musical, earned widespread acclaim for its brutally honest exploration of identity and artistry. Meanwhile, revivals of established Pulitzer winners—including Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, and Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**—demonstrated the continuing relevance of American theatrical classics.

Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt** brought deeply personal Holocaust storytelling to Broadway, while Jordan E. Cooper's **Ain't No Mo'** pushed boundaries with provocative satire. The 10 featured productions average an impressive 83/100 critical score, reflecting a year of exceptional artistic achievement.

Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection represents some of the most critically acclaimed theatrical experiences of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the plays that opened during Broadway's 2023 season continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions, averaging an impressive 82/100 critic score, showcases the breadth and vitality of contemporary American theatre—from bold revivals of classic works to innovative new voices pushing the medium forward.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's transformative revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has definitively redeemed Stephen Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop through emotionally resonant performances that finally unlock the show's backward-moving narrative. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that intellectual property adaptations can transcend mere fan service, with critics praising its technical innovation and theatrical craftsmanship. Meanwhile, **Appropriate** stands out as a searing family drama that critics have embraced as a modern masterpiece, anchored by Sarah Paulson's commanding performance.

The season's diversity is striking: alongside these headliners, audiences find everything from Ossie Davis's bracingly relevant 1961 satire **Purlie Victorious** to Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us**, which chronicles his infiltration of a white nationalist meeting with both humor and insight. Timely revivals of **Parade** and **Sweeney Todd** sit alongside Pulitzer Prize winner **Fat Ham**, a raucous Hamlet adaptation set at a Black family barbecue, and Jodie Comer's tour-de-force debut in **Prima Facie**.

Whether you're drawn to musical theatre legends, contemporary social commentary, or virtuosic solo performances, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the plays that defined Broadway's 2023 season and continue to resonate with audiences today.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This curated selection of ten productions maintains an impressive average critic score of 84/100, reflecting a particularly strong theatrical season that has resonated with both reviewers and audiences.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band, which critics consistently praise as a theatrical marvel for its authentic portrayal of the creative process. The production's meticulous attention to period detail and its exploration of artistic collaboration have established it as one of the most discussed plays of recent seasons.

Musical theater also shows exceptional range during this period. **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a remarkably original work, with its charming story of robot romance earning praise for emotional depth that transcends its unconventional premise. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist, proves that bold comedic risks can yield substantial critical rewards.

The season also features noteworthy revivals, including George C. Wolfe's production of **Gypsy** with Audra McDonald offering a fresh interpretation of the iconic Mama Rose, and a lavish staging of **Oliver!** that balances spectacle with Dickensian grit.

From experimental dance-musicals like **Illinoise** to intimate dramas such as **Mary Jane**, the diversity of voices and styles represented in these ten productions reflects Broadway's ongoing evolution. Whether you're drawn to innovative reimaginings, original works, or classic revivals, these critically acclaimed shows offer compelling reasons to experience live theater.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through the spring of 2026, the season showcases an impressive array of productions that opened throughout 2025, ranging from bold new works to reimagined classics. This month's top ten plays reflect a theater landscape balancing artistic ambition with crowd-pleasing entertainment, earning an average critic score of 84 out of 100.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. The Dutch director's stripped-down approach to Arthur Miller's classic proves that powerful staging can amplify rather than overshadow timeless material. Close behind, **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** returns to Broadway with a 20th-anniversary revival that critics describe as joyous and perfectly timed, demonstrating the enduring appeal of well-crafted musical comedy.

The season's diversity is evident in the range of offerings: **Paddington The Musical** enchants audiences with its remarkably lifelike puppet work, while Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** brings smart, sensitive observations about language and identity to the stage. Family dramas feature prominently, with both **Liberation** and **Purpose** earning praise for their ambitious explorations of memory, feminism, and generational conflict. Meanwhile, **Dead Outlaw** and **Buena Vista Social Club** offer musical experiences at opposite ends of the spectrum—one a darkly comic rock score about a bizarre historical footnote, the other a celebration of Cuban musical heritage.

Whether seeking innovative directorial visions, heartfelt revivals, or ambitious new American plays, this month's selections offer compelling reasons to experience live theater.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings an intimate start to the year's new Broadway plays, with quality taking precedence over quantity as the season begins to unfold.

Leading the current lineup is **Every Brilliant Thing**, an interactive solo performance starring Daniel Radcliffe that earns an impressive 80/100 from critics. The production tackles the weighty subject of depression through an unexpectedly life-affirming lens, cataloging the small moments that make existence worthwhile. Radcliffe's performance draws consistent praise for its warmth and accessibility, with the show's participatory format breaking down the traditional barriers between performer and audience. Critics note his ability to navigate both the humor and heartbreak inherent in the material, creating an experience that feels both deeply personal and universally resonant.

While this month features just one new play opening in 2026, it sets a promising tone for the year ahead. The strong critical reception—with an 80/100 average—suggests that Broadway producers are prioritizing carefully crafted productions over saturating the market. This focused approach allows theatergoers to engage more deeply with individual works rather than feeling overwhelmed by choices.

The emphasis on solo performance and interactive storytelling in **Every Brilliant Thing** also reflects broader trends in contemporary theater, where audiences increasingly seek intimate, immersive experiences that challenge conventional staging.

As the spring season progresses, this early showing indicates that 2026 may be remembered for thoughtful, character-driven work rather than spectacle alone. Check back regularly as more productions open and the year's theatrical landscape continues to take shape.
